status: candidate / pending_human_review (model reading, round 21 second round; not an operator gate)
dataset_family: Fuzhou community T2DM cohort followed at Fujian Medical University Union Hospital (Endocrinology), screened January 2019 and reassessed January 2022 (ethics 2023KY165). Of 328 screened, 234 were analysed (75 with hypoglycaemia, 159 controls). The DR analysis is nested in the 75 hypoglycaemic patients (44 MCI / 31 NCI). No other corpus block reports this cohort.
method_family: Retrospective longitudinal cohort with a nested case-control comparison. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression of clinical risk factors, one of them a baseline binary diabetic-retinopathy grade from funduscopy by a retinal specialist (ETDRS criteria), with a per-factor ROC. No retinal image analysis, no quantitative retinal measure, no classifier.
what_it_shows:
Gao R, Zhan M, Ke S, Wu K, He G, Qi L, Liu X, Liu X, Wang L, Liu L (2024), Diabetes Research and Clinical Practice 207:111036.
- Population: 75 T2DM patients aged 45-75 with documented hypoglycaemia.
- DR at baseline was more common in those with MCI at the 3-year assessment: 52.3% vs 22.6%, P = 0.010.
- DR remained associated after multivariable adjustment: aOR 3.078 (95% CI 1.158-12.358), P = 0.029.
- The authors give an AUC of 0.678 for retinopathy predicting MCI and call it 'moderate but not high accuracy'. Grip strength had the highest AUC (0.730).
why:
IDENTITY. The PDF's title, authors (Ruonan Gao ... Lijing Wang, Libin Liu; Department of Endocrinology, Fujian Medical University Union Hospital) and DOI 10.1016/j.diabres.2023.111036 match the block header and author list. P-5's first author is a different Gao (Hebei Gao, Wenzhou). I read the whole extract, pp.1-7, up to the References.

STATED FORM, partly. What it shows: a retinal-structure finding, made by an ocular examination done for this study (funduscopy by a retinal specialist graded to ETDRS criteria, p.2), is associated within the study with MCI three years later, after adjustment. That is part of the retinal leg. What it does not show:
(a) Population. It covers only T2DM patients with hypoglycaemia, 75 people, not early cognitive decline in general.
(b) What is measured. The marker is the presence of a diabetic microvascular complication, not a retinal biomarker of neurodegeneration. A shared systemic microvascular process is a plausible explanation that the design cannot separate, much as the stroke confound does in P-952. The authors themselves attribute the link to shared neuro- and microvascular pathways (p.5).
(c) Detection. The DR-only discrimination is weak (AUC 0.678, p.6), and no validation is attempted.
(d) Scalability is not tested, and eye movement is not examined.

ADDITIONAL CAVEATS FROM THE SOURCE. The numerical ones are my arithmetic, not the authors'.
(1) Baseline status. MCI was diagnosed only at the 2022 assessment ('Cognitive function assessments were conducted at the end of January 2022', p.2). Baseline MoCA scores were collected (Table 1), but baseline MCI is not listed as an exclusion; only prevalent dementia is. 'Developing MCI 3 years later' may therefore include prevalent MCI.
(2) Measurement bias. Visual difficulty from DR could lower MoCA scores. The authors switch to MoCA-B only when a DR patient reports difficulty seeing the figures (p.2).
(3) Crude odds ratio. From the Table 3 counts (MCI 23 DR / 21 no DR; NCI 7 / 24) the crude OR is 3.76, but Table 4 prints a univariate OR of 2.775.
(4) Univariate p. The univariate CI 1.042-7.508 implies p of about 0.04, not the printed 0.012.
(5) Adjusted CI. The adjusted CI 1.158-12.358 is not symmetric on the log scale around 3.078; its geometric centre is about 3.78.
(6) AUC. For a binary predictor with sensitivity 23/44 and specificity 24/31, the AUC is about 0.65, not 0.678.
(7) Model size. The multivariable model has about 10 covariates (Table 4 footnote) against 31 non-events, so it is overfitted and the CI is very wide.
The authors concede a single city and a small sample (p.6).

NARROWED FORM, partly. The study fits the head clause, 'ocular measures show preliminary, single-centre associations with MCI': it is a single centre, gives an adjusted association, and is not validated. It does not fit the retinal sub-clause, 'retinal imaging (fundus with or without OCT) discriminated MCI', for three reasons. The measure is a clinical DR grade, not imaging analysed for MCI. The population is diabetic patients with hypoglycaemia. The discrimination is weak. Admitting it would also require the wording to name diabetic retinopathy in T2DM as a risk-factor association, which is a different claim from a retinal biomarker of cognitive decline. The verdict is partly, not yes, because the population and the measure both differ from what the wording describes.

INDEPENDENCE. A single Fuzhou centre. No shared sample, site or authors with P-5, P-952, P-966 or P-105. None with the round-1 candidates: P-1152 (Morocco T2DM), P-255 (EU RECOGNISED T2D) and the rest. None with the round-2 candidate P-270 (Xiangya, Changsha). Not a preprint: a peer-reviewed Elsevier article.

quotes.quote: Multivariate logistic analysis showed that low grip strength, existing diabetic retinopathy (DR), and multiple hypoglycemia episodes were associated with higher odds of MCI in patients with hypoglycemia (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 0.909 [95 % CI 0.859–0.963]), 3.078 [95 % CI 1.158–12.358], and 4.642 [95 % CI 1.284–16.776], respectively, all P < 0.05).

Cognitive function assessments were conducted at the end of January 2022. To evaluate potential predictors for hypoglycemia-associated MCI, patients with hypoglycemia were further categorized into non-cognitive impairment (NCI) and MCI groups based on the cognitive evaluations conducted at the end of the study.

Funduscopic examination was performed by a retinal specialist to evaluate the presence of retinopathy based on the criteria of Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy. The findings were categorized into normal retina or diabetic retinopathy (DR; including non-proliferative DR and proliferative DR).

For the items related to visuospatial/executive functions, patients with DR were asked if they had difficulty seeing the figures on the MoCA questionnaire. If they reported difficulty, the MoCA-B version was used.

In the multivariate logistic analysis adjusted for clinically relevant variables, low grip strength and existing DR remained associated with higher odds of developing MCI 3 years later (adjusted ORs 0.909 [95 % CI 0.859–0.963] (P = 0.001) and 3.078 [95 % CI 1.158–12.358] (P = 0.029), respectively).
ROC curve analysis (Supplementary Fig. 1) revealed that low grip strength exhibited the strongest predictive value for MCI in patients with hypoglycemia among all the risk factors (AUC = 0.730).
